evidence.field: A00355-003 research note; variant relationship 歬/前
evidence.text: The entry treats 歬 as a variant of 前 and quotes Shuowen: 歬 means moving forward and is formed from 止 over 舟. It also records a competing traditional explanation: 刀+歬 was the graph for cutting evenly, later written 前 in clerical form; 歬 was then used for the directional word. Guangyun is cited as calling 歬 an old form of 前. This source reports competing historical lexicographic accounts; it does not resolve which graph was first.

evidence.text: The entry lists bronze forms, Chu manuscripts, Qin manuscripts, Shuowen seal form and Han clerical form; its visible bronze examples include Western Zhou middle and late inscriptions.
